Carla Nguyen: Quick sync note  R3 Optimize toolkit scope. We need a pragmatic split: batching (runtime risk), cache hints (low risk), quant recs (advisory), eval-triggered alerts (pilot). Lock by EOD.
Omar Velez: Agree. Customers want measurable wins not theory. Recommend prioritize batching heuristics that are reversible. Two safe heuristics: sticky-prefix batching and opportunistic micro-batching.
Hannah Brooks: Sticky-prefix sounds good for conversation apps. Micro-batching good for high-throughput inference. Need to define SLO rollback thresholds (p99 delta).
Marco Diaz: For quant recs keep them advisory only — provide presets (fp16, q8-lite) with expected savings and risk note. Customers requested a one-line rationale and an audit row. That should be lightweight enough.
Carla Nguyen: Acceptance criteria proposal: 1) Pilot w/3 customers, 2) Console shows per-route token delta + latency deltas, 3) p99 regression <= 10% for customers who enable batching, 4) recommendation adoption metric tracked.
Omar Velez: Telemetry plan: emit events opt_toolkit.rule_evaluated, rule_suggested, rule_accepted, alert_triggered. Need sample sizes to estimate precision for eval-alerts.
Hannah Brooks: Eval-alert MVP = read-only signals in Console. No automated rollbacks or pruning. Keep thresholds conservative to avoid noisy alerts.
Marco Diaz: Compliance/fin-reg asks: exportable audit logs (CSV/JSON) and short template rationale for each recommendation: "Why: <expected saving> / Risk: <brief>". We can generate from rule metadata, not model introspection.
Carla Nguyen: Owners: runtime = Omar, telemetry/infra = Marco, Console = Hannah. Timeline (4 weeks): Week 1 spec + rule schema, Week 2 runtime prototype + perf baseline, Week 3 telemetry + console stub, Week 4 pilot rollouts + metrics review.
eng-bot: Poll posted: "R3 priority order" options: [Batching, Cache hints, Quant advisories, Eval-alerts]. Vote: https://redwood.internal/poll/9912
Omar Velez: Vote: Batching > Cache hints > Eval-alerts > Quant.
Hannah Brooks: Note blocker: kernel batching changes need perf runs and eng-runtime time. If blocked, we can ship heuristic in user-space scheduler first.
Marco Diaz: Pilot gating: per-customer feature flags + opt-in acceptance. Add runbook for noisy alerts and a contact for escalation.
Carla Nguyen: Final call: R3 MVP = batching heuristics (opt-in, reversible), cache hints + quant recs as advisories, eval-triggered alerts read-only. Proceed with owners/timeline above unless objections. :thumbsup:
Omar Velez: +1
Hannah Brooks: +1
Marco Diaz: +1
